Judicial Branch Ends Attorney Entry Screening Bypass Program and  Announces Procedure for Reimbursement
Date:
11/17/2026
Beginning January 1, 2027, attorneys entering state courthouses will no longer be able to bypass security screening. Attorneys who show their bar cards (which can be downloaded from the Board of Bar Overseers website) will be able to go to the head of the screening line.  In some courthouses, there may be a separate "attorneys only" line if resources allow.
Chief Justice Stanfill spoke to the policy change: The Judicial Branch continuously reviews our security protocols to ensure appropriate measures are in place.  We believe this policy change provides greater protection for all people using the courthouse. The policy change follows best practices for courthouse security and aligns with the policy of the federal courts in Maine and the state courts of most other New England states.
The Judicial Branch stopped issuing security cards to attorneys in May 2026. Attorneys whose security cards have not expired by January 1, 2027, will be able to receive a pro rata refund of the fee for the unexpired portion. Instructions and the form for requesting a refund are posted on the For Attorneys page of the Judicial Branch website and can be downloaded directly here:
https://www.courts.maine.gov/attorneys/atty-security-card-reimbursement.pdf

Judicial Branch Issues Amendment to Administrative Order on the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS), Effective November 2, 2026
Date:
11/2/2026
The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that an Administrative Order on rules and procedures applicable to Maine eCourts and eFiling has been amended regarding the use of non-Judicial Branch court forms when one has been provided by the court.
AO JB 20-03 (A. 11-26)
was adopted in 2020 to provide guidance on the applicability of the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) during the transitional period during the implementation of Maine eCourts and electronic filing when there are conflicts between MRECS and other Judicial Branch rules and administrative orders.
New Section I.C. of JB 20-20 provides that "[i]f an applicable court-approved form exists and is available to the public, the parties must use it" and further adds the following requirement:
"If a filer does not use a form, the filer must include a brief explanation in a cover letter accompanying the submission that indicates the existing form is not suitable."
Barbara Cardone, Director of Legal Affairs and Public Relations explained the reason for the amendment. "The reason for the amendment is to increase the efficiency of reviewing eFiling submissions. eFilers who submit non-Judicial Branch-approved court forms can avoid having their submission rejected by including an explanatory cover letter with the eFiling. We hope this clarification helps the eFiling and legal community's smooth transition to eFiling and Maine eCourts."
AO JB 20-03 (A. 11-26) has been posted on the Administrative Orders page of the Judicial Branch website at
https://www.courts.maine.gov/adminorders/index.html

STATE OF MAINE       SUPERIOR COURT 
DISTRICT COURT 
 
  
STANDING ORDER REQUIRING 
PAPER FILING FOR ELECTION DAY 
2026 EMERGENCY MATTERS 
 
 
 The Maine Judicial Branch (MJB) is implementing the Maine eCourts 
system – including eFiling – statewide.1  EFileMaine is a practical and efficient 
document submission system already in use in many courts throughout the 
state.  However, because filings related to Election Day may be uniquely time-
sensitive, to ensure timely processing, the MJB will require paper filing under 
the limited circumstances described below.   
 
 It is therefore ORDERED that any emergency Title 21-A filings related to 
Election Day 2026 filed between 4:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026, and 
9:00 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, must be by paper, unless otherwise 
ordered.2 
 
It is further ORDERED that the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems 
are SUSPENDED to the extent necessary to give effect to this order.   
 
 
 
Dated: 10/28/2026   _____/s/______________________   
       Chief Justice Robert E. Mullen 
 
 
 
Dated: 10/28/2026   ___/s/_______________________   
       Chief Judge Brent Davis 
 
1 Further information about the Maine eCourts system is available at 
https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

day after the election.

Supreme Judicial Court to Hold Oral Arguments at Three Maine High Schools

Date: 9/29/2026

The Supreme Judicial Court will hold court and hear a total of nine cases at three Maine high schools next week.

On Tuesday, October 6, beginning at 9:00 a.m., the Court will visit Katahdin Middle/High School in Stacyville to hear arguments in three appellate cases. Senator Trey Stewart extended the invitation to the Law Court. The three cases are scheduled to begin at 9:00 a.m., 10:00 a.m., and 11:00 a.m.

The Court will hear three appeals at Morse High School in Bath on Wednesday, October 7 at the invitation of Senator Denise Tepler. The Court will follow the same schedule with the first oral argument starting at 9:00 a.m., the second at 10:00 a.m., and the third at 11:00 a.m.

And on Thursday, October 8, the Court will hear three cases at Kennebunk High School at the invitation of Representative Daniel Sayre. Again, the schedule indicates that the first case starts at 9:00 a.m.

Students receive copies of the briefs in advance and, after each argument, the lawyers stay to answer questions from interested students. When the cases are decided, the schools receive a link to the decisions to share with the students.

Beginning in 2005, the Court has held oral arguments in actual appellate cases at over 40 Maine high schools around the state. In each school, the gymnasium, cafeteria, or auditorium is turned into a courtroom for the morning so that the students can observe the appellate process. The Court has visited schools from York County to Aroostook County; from Oxford County to Washington County; and many places in between.

Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill said, "We hope that providing real-time exposure to the third branch of government supplements the students' civics education and exposes Maine learners to the concept of justice. The practice of appellate law is rarely seen on television or in the movies. Creating a courtroom environment in a high school takes great effort on the part of the school administration and staff and we appreciate their extensive efforts."

The press is welcome to attend. The case schedule has been posted on the Courts website here.

Live video streaming of these cases, and all other Supreme Judicial Court oral arguments, is available here.

If interviews or photographs are desired while the Court is at the schools, please contact Julie Finn beforehand to schedule an interview at the below email address. Photographs and video of students are subject to the rules of the high school, and the press is requested to contact school officials directly.

Date:
9/10/2026
Supreme Judicial Court Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill and members of the Supreme Judicial Court will conduct a student-teacher town hall on Thursday, September 17, 2026, to commemorate the 239th anniversary of the signing of the U.S. Constitution.
"The Constitution is the bedrock and framework of American democracy," said Chief Justice Stanfill. "It shapes the everyday lives of young Americans, including their individual rights and freedoms, now, and in the future. We hope the student town hall will spark conversation and curiosity about the role and importance of the Constitution in establishing the U.S. as a nation based on the rule of law."
Classes and students are invited to attend and participate by Zoom or in person at the Capital Judicial Center in Augusta. Classes wishing to attend in person should RSVP to Julia.Finn@courts.maine.gov by Wednesday, September 16 at 5:00 p.m.

items.content_text:
STATE OF MAINE 
SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT 
STANDING ORDER REGARDING  
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER JB-24-03 
PILOT PROGRAM TO CONDITIONALLY AUTHORIZE  
LAW STUDENT EXTERNS TO PROVIDE 
PUBLIC DEFENSE SERVICES 
 
Effective: September 4, 2026 
 
 On December 18, 2024, the Supreme Judicial Court adopted 
Administrative Order JB-24-03, Pilot Program to Conditionally Authorize Law 
Student Externs to Provide Public Defense Services.  The order provides that it 
expires on September 5, 2026. 
 
 The Court has not determined whether to adopt the program 
permanently.  There are, however, students enrolled in externships for the fall 
semester of 2026 who will be unable to participate in the externships if the 
order is allowed to expire.  
 
 Because it will take time to determine whether the program will be made 
permanent, but the Court does not wish to prevent the currently enrolled 
students from participating in their externships, it is hereby ORDERED that the 
effective term of the pilot program established by Administrative Order JB-24-
03 is extended through January 15, 2027.   
 
 The University of Maine School of Law and the organizations hosting 
student externs should not arrange for student externs for the spring semester 
of 2027 without first confirming that the pilot program will remain in effect for 
that semester. 
 
 Dated: September 4, 2026   For the Court: 
 
 
 
         /s/     
        Valerie Stanfill 
        Chief Justice
